prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Personalize Your Pet's Adoption Certificate", "Select Pet Personality Trait", "Companion Name"]
1: ["Desktop Pet Quick Reference", "Here is how to interact with your pet once it lands on your screen.", "Drag & Drop anywhere on screen", "Right-click pet for settings & hide option"]
2: ["Choose Your Companion's World", "Preview Path Journey"]
3: ["Setting Up Desktop Pet Workspace", "Calibrating pet movement bounds and desktop graphics layer...", "Preparing companion assets"]
4: ["Returning user? Sign in with your original account to instantly sync your saved pet and progress."]
5: ["Every path unlocks exclusive desktop companion accessories and starter items.", "View Path Perks"]
6: ["If your pet doesn't appear on screen immediately, check your system tray icon."]
7: ["Upload Pet Photo Reference", "Upload bright, front-facing photos for the best custom desktop pet rendering.", "Photo Quality Checklist"]
8: ["Your Companion Has Arrived!", "Your pet is now active on your desktop screen. Click and drag your pet to move it around or right-click for quick actions.", "Meet My Pet"]
9: ["You can adopt additional companions later from your desktop pet collection.", "Most Popular Choice"]

verdicts.problem: Mentions free extras and exclusive perks
Pressures the user using popularity framing
